what: Independent design review of the draft of Addendum 8 before it came into force. Four reviewers, one lens each. The first attempt at the statistics and implementation lenses was stopped by a usage limit; both were run again on another model against the revised draft.

findings.title: R3's control on held-out B omits three budgets generation 0 has already been run at (38 sound, the study knows 39), and R3 is still scored when C1new is not run
findings.problem: Draft R3: the final student at 10^4 has more sound held-out B solves than generation 0 'at any budget run there', listed as 10^4, 10^5, 413,254, 1,126,452 and C1new. Generation 0 (S+C+f+R) has also been run there at 181,775, 251,479 and 569,881, and the 181,775 run holds a sound solve none of the listed rungs has. The README already quotes 39 over seven budgets; confirm.py will compare with 38. The frozen variant is at 50 verified after two cycles (about 39-40 sound at the usual 0.8 ratio), so R3, the criterion every earlier loop failed, can turn on this one task. Second gap: when C1new > 1,700,000 the rung is skipped but R3 is still returned True/False (and P11 scored) from the smaller rungs. That happens for T_new > 562.2M; the frozen constants allow up to 1,191.4M (12 cycles x 99.0M + 3.38M).
findings.evidence: <work>/control-fairness/t3_heldB_union.py (stored programs, audit only, no solver) printed: sound by budget 22, 35, 36 (181,775), 37, 37, 37, 37; 'union over the rungs the draft's R3 names: 38'; 'union over all seven budgets: 39'; 'only at a budget the draft leaves out: fresh2/((modulo-k ... 10) (identify-is-mod-k ... 3)) | budgets [181775]'. confirm.py line 59 HELD_RUNGS = {C1old: 413_254, C2old: 1_126_452}; lines 215-219 skip C1new above MEMORY_LIMIT; line 436 'R3': len(new@student) > len(held_any) regardless of line 437 'R3_covers_the_cumulative_budget'. a7_amortise.py: C1new = 1,700,000 at T_new = 562.2M, 3,561,538 at the maximum. Checked and fine: C1new = T_new/338 + 36,686 is above the original accounting (T_new/338), so when it is run the draft's R3 is at least as strict as the original.
findings.proposed_change: Add 181,775, 251,479 and 569,881 to HELD_RUNGS (124 tasks, 124M candidates of ceiling in all) and name all seven budgets plus C1new in R3. Make R3 (and its prediction) 'not scored' when C1new exceeds the memory limit, instead of True/False. The loop is deterministic and the registered run repeats the development run, so write T_new, C1new and whether C1new is run into the registration as numbers before it comes into force.

findings.title: The equal-cost rung shrinks with the size of the set (C2new = 10^5 + T_new/1,000); the control's top rung is one at which generation 0 was still gaining on FRESH-3
findings.problem: C2new is exact arithmetic (1,000 x C2new = T_new + 10^8, both at ceilings), but the training charge per task is T_new/N and N = 1,000 was chosen after Addendum 7 failed at N = 300. For T_new = 3 x 10^8 the 'whole budget' is 400,000 per task here and 1,100,000 at FRESH-3's size. Addendum 7's own class turned on exactly this: the same trained state is 'established' against generation 0 up to the budget that N = 1,000 would have given and 'not established' against the registered one. The draft keeps 524,267, but on FRESH-3 (the population FRESH-4 comes from) generation 0 was not flat there, so 'any budget' and ending 3 ('reach beyond the budget') stop inside the range where the control was still improving. The claim sentence and the licence do not say that training is amortised over 1,000 tasks.
findings.evidence: <work>/control-fairness/a7_amortise.py on results/replication.json: trained at 10^5 against the union of generation 0 up to 228,969: 71 against 57, 23 to 9, p = 0.01003; up to 524,267: 71 against 64, 18 to 11, p = 0.13247. C2 for T_old: N = 300 gives 524,267, N = 1,000 gives 227,280. T_new = 110,739,887 (first variant) gives C2new 210,740, below C2old; 300M gives 400,000 (1,100,000 at N = 300); the maximum 1,191.4M gives 1,291,400, inside the memory limit. a4_frontier.py: generation 0 on FRESH-3, sound, new to the union by rung: 45, +10, +2, +7 (union 64); 7 of the 61 sound solves of the 524,267 run needed more than 228,969 candidates (5 of them by fusion, whose pools grow with the budget). On held-out B it was flat from 251,479 to 1,126,452 (37, 37, 37, 37).
findings.proposed_change: Add one generation-0 rung on FRESH-4 at 1,126,452 (Addendum 7's top rung, already run with four workers; about 6 x 10^8 candidates spent, roughly two hours at Addendum 7's rate), put it in the 'any budget' union and read ending 3 at it. Or register the rule min(1,700,000, T_new/300 + 10^5). State in the claim and the licence that training is charged at T_new/1,000 per task, and print C2 at N = 300 beside C2new. T_new is known from the development run: write the rungs as numbers.

findings.title: The R2 rows pass on a one-directional count of one task: (a) ignores the other direction, soundness and symbol use; (b) drops descendants that work without their ancestor
findings.problem: (a) counts verified teacher solves that generation 0 lacks at the same budget, and R2 needs only one. It does not look at tasks generation 0 solves and the teacher does not, at whether the teacher's program is sound or uses a learned symbol, or at whether generation 0 failed for lack of reach or at a rejected first match. (b) removes the first cycle's symbols together with every symbol whose definition names one. A descendant's witness is a closed base-language term and works without its ancestor, so a lost solve can rest on a later cycle's own symbol (the draft's reverse / append-k case), which the README scored 'no' for an earlier loop. 'First made after the first cycle' subtracts only student0 and the last student of cycle 1, not the other runs of cycle 1. The two parts are not tied to the same task or symbol. By this rule an earlier loop whose registered R2 verdict is 'no' passes.
findings.evidence: <work>/control-fairness/t1_loop.py then t5_r2.py (tiny loop, exposed partitions, budgets <= 2000, 2 workers): 'cycle 2: teacher solved 23, generation 0 at the same budget on the same 142 tasks solved 33; confirm.py's count not_by_generation_0_at_that_budget = 1; the other direction = 11'; the one task is far/is-odds, 'used [s4_1]', 'gen0: rejected match'. t7_sound.py: that program is 'sound by the audit: False', counterexample [7, 19, 3, 15, 26, 15, 33]. So (a) is met where the symbols cost the teacher ten solves. (b) in the same run: lost 7, gained by dropping 2 (flips both ways). a6_expertB_r2.py, the draft's rule on the stored Expert B loop: (b) 'lost 23, first solved after cycle 1: 8 -> met', (a) 18 and 21 teacher-only tasks; README verdict table for that loop: R2 'no'; 5 of the 8 use only a built-on symbol and dropping the built-on symbols alone loses 0 of 147. expert_ablate.py lines 8-9: 'A symbol defined on a dropped symbol keeps working'. confirm.py lines 273-277, 413-434.
findings.proposed_change: (a) Count a task only if the teacher's program is sound, its recorded 'used' list is not empty and generation 0's run on it ended without a public match; print the reverse count and require the first to exceed it. (b) Add one row: the final vocabulary without the first cycle's symbols, descendants kept (338 tasks at 10^4). Count a lost solve only if its final program uses a dropped symbol and no run up to the end of cycle 1 solved it. Report both ablations and say which one R2(b) reads. In the write-up re-score the earlier loops by the same rule or say that the rule changed.

findings.title: 'New against old' is at equal deployment budget only, and 'old against the union up to its own C2' is not the comparison of Addendum 7
findings.problem: Ending 2 and D5 ('and more than the earlier loop') compare the two vocabularies at 10^5 with training ceilings T_new and 127,280,000 that are not equalised; the wording does not say so. The secondary 'old against the union up to its own C2 (the comparison of Addendum 7 again, on these tasks)' stops at 227,280, because N = 1,000. That is Addendum 7's mid rung, not its control (524,267), and there the same state already had p = 0.010 against 0.13 at its registered control. A significant result would read as a replication of a comparison that was never the registered one. D6 uses the same label for the 'any budget' comparison. The code matches the draft (old_own = student, equal, C2old), with one hole: it names rungs instead of taking every rung up to C2old, so if T_new < T_old (the first variant: 110,739,887) the C2new rung would be left out.
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md lines 662-664, 676-678, 727-728. confirm.py line 316: old_own = union of controls 'student', 'equal', 'C2old'. <work>/control-fairness/a7_amortise.py: C2 for T_old at N = 1,000 is 227,280 (mid rung of Addendum 7: 228,969); union up to 228,969: p = 0.01003; up to 524,267: p = 0.13247; first-variant T gives C2new 210,740 < 227,280. replicate.py line 247 and confirm.py line 234 build 'trained' and 'old' the same way (spec_without on the same library), so the arm itself is the Addendum 7 state.
findings.proposed_change: Word ending 2 and D5 as 'more than the earlier loop's vocabulary at the same deployment budget (training ceilings T_new against 127,280,000)'. If an equal-cost reading is wanted, add one row: old at 10^5 + (T_new - T_old)/1,000 when that is positive. Call the secondary 'old against generation 0 up to 227,280, its cost-equal budget on 1,000 tasks (Addendum 7's control went to 524,267)' and keep 'the comparison of Addendum 7 on more tasks' for D6 only. Build old_own from every rung with budget <= C2old.

reviews.coverage:
All scripts and outputs are in <work>/control-fairness. FRESH-4 was not generated or touched; solvers ran only on exposed partitions and FRESH-3 at budgets <= 2000 with 2 workers. Nothing was checked at real budgets.

Checked and held:
- T_new. In a tiny instrumented loop (t1_loop.py) the sum of budget x jobs over every Harness.run call equals training_ceiling (1,471,800 both; 18 runs, 18 timeline rows). It covers teacher runs at share x unsolved, every trial at 214 + dreams, the dream baseline and the report runs. No task exceeded its budget. verdicts_read = 2,645 = 11 x 214 + 149 + 142.
- Uncounted driver work. Dreamer at the registered constants on the 154-program corpus of the Addendum 7 loop (t2_dreamer.py, no solver): 1,062 programs x 300 pool inputs = 318,600 single-input evaluations, 58M interpreter steps, 42 s per cycle. That is about 13,000 candidate-equivalents (24 points per candidate), 0.4% of one trial's ceiling and under 0.2M over 12 cycles. compress.propose took 11 calls and 2 s in the tiny loop and evaluates only nullary witnesses. Negligible in candidates; visible in seconds, which the draft reports.
- Same machinery. The spec confirm.py rebuilds from the report equals the loop's own spec for the final vocabulary (abstractions and constants equal, keep None, vocabulary restored, components SCfR). It reproduced the loop's final student on the learning tasks program for program (76 and 76). Generation 0 is the same spec with an empty library; 'old' is built as replicate.py built 'trained'. 'New' carries no cut vocabulary and no constants from training other than learned nullary symbols.
- Budget actually spent. In all nine rows of results/replication.json every run without a public match spent exactly its ceiling and no record is above its budget (a1_rows.py, t7_sound.py). Generation 0 at 524,267 on FRESH-3 spent 56.9% of the ceiling because 149 runs stopped at a first match: 61 sound, 88 not sound with 89% of the budget left. The trained state at 10^5 lost 84 the same way, so the first-match rule is symmetric.
- Route split. Trace at budget 2000 on 150 FRESH-3 tasks (t6_routes.py, instrumented copy of hybrid.py): where no match is found the direct route gets 86% of the budget when S does not apply and 37% when S applies and fails, minimum 13%, as the formula says. The plain registered engine run to 10^6 solves soundly nothing on held-out B outside generation 0's union (t4_registered.py: 0 extra), so the split does not visibly starve the control.
- The union. It gives the control about three times the trained arm's charge (for C2new = 400,000 the five rungs sum to 1.26M per task) and five first matches and verifier queries per task. I found nothing fairer to pre-register, apart from the top rung (finding 2) and the omitted held-out B budgets (finding 1).
- Formulas. C2old = 227,280; C2new, C1new and old_own are computed as the text says; kinds_of reads generation 0 at its largest rung; teacher3 and teacher_final of the Addendum 7 loop (same vocabulary, same budget) are identical program for program (a3_flips.py).

Seen outside my lens, not a finding here: confirm.predictions() scores P1-P12, which are not the draft's D1-D11. D9 and D11 have no scorer, and P1, P2 and P11 score things the draft says are not predictions.

findings.title: Ending 4 ('no dream computed it') removes only the dreams that happened to be sampled; half of FRESH-4 is an exact composition of two learning tasks
findings.problem: confirm.py's dreamt() counts a FRESH-4 task only when a stored dream program reproduces its 16 examples. Two things make that too narrow. (1) 517 of the 1,000 tasks are, on all 16 examples, ref_B(ref_A(x)) for two LEARNING tasks A and B (424 because both stage instances are learning-task functions). They all lie in the space the Dreamer samples; the rule catches only the few that 400 dreams per cycle happen to hit. (2) Compression anti-unifies parameters (the old library's caesar symbol and the toy run's identify-k symbol are examples), so a dream of the same routine pair with other parameters supports the same symbols. The gate sample that breaks ties is disjoint from the corpus sample only by exact behaviour. As drafted, ending 4 and D8 repeat the primary test on about 95% of the set, and the outcome string would say 'also on the tasks no dream of the loop computed' for tasks made of the very routine pairs the dreams were made of.
findings.evidence:
Scripts and logs in <work>/confounds. No solver ran on FRESH-4 and no solver-made program was evaluated on a FRESH-4 example; dreams were compared with FRESH-4 through the reference functions of their two learning tasks.
- b_overlap.py: 'FRESH-4 tasks whose 16 examples equal ref_B(ref_A(x)) for some pair of learning tasks (A, B): 517 | with A and B both solved by the Addendum-7 loop: 177'; 'same FUNCTION on the 866-input FRESH pool as a learning task: both 424 | first only 426 | second only 74 | neither 76'; 'same routine FAMILY as a learning task: both 881 | first only 59 | second only 58 | neither 2'. Same numbers with only the first validated reading (b_overlap_first.py).
- c_dream_sim.py (deepen.Dreamer itself, on the 154 verified learning programs of results/replication.json as a stand-in corpus, 100 gate + 300 corpus dreams per cycle): 'cycle 1: FRESH-4 tasks some dream computes (by reference) 29 | whose routine pair some dream composed 191'; 'cycle 4: 64 | 335'; 'routine pair the Dreamer COULD compose from this corpus: 446'. The deepening loop's corpus is larger, so its pair-level numbers will be higher.
- h_propose.py: 'gate dreams whose ROUTINE PAIR also occurs in the corpus sample: 39 of 100 | whose inner task or outer task occurs in a corpus dream: 99 | identical (f, g) task pairs: 0'.
- g_misc.py: the stored dream programs parse back (108 of 108 from a toy loop) and dreamt() fires on FRESH-3 stand-ins (3 exact, 23 by routine pair), so the machinery works; the rule is what is narrow.
findings.proposed_change: Exact rule, computed from the loop report alone. In confirm.py, next to dreamt_keys: dream_pairs = {(partitions.family(f.split('/',1)[1]), partitions.family(g.split('/',1)[1])) for cycle in report['cycles'] for group in cycle['dream_programs'].values() for _, f, g in group}. A task is 'dreamt' if (a) a dream program reproduces its 16 examples, as now, or (b) (task.stages[0][0], task.stages[1][0]) is in dream_pairs. Ending 4 and D8 are read on the tasks in neither set; (a), (b) and both comparisons are reported. Also report, deciding nothing, the primary comparison on the tasks outside the dream space: those with a stage routine for which no run of the loop holds a verified learning program (families read off the timeline's 'programs'). In 'What FRESH-4 is and is not', state that 517 of 1,000 tasks are exact compositions of two learning tasks. Re-make D8 for the new stratum. Per accepted symbol, print whether it was accepted on the tie-break and its real_tasks (already stored in 'proposed'), and count the new-only solves that use a symbol with real_tasks = 0.

findings.title: FRESH-4 pairs up the loop's own learning tasks (first stage in 850 tasks, some stage in 924); the registration does not say so and reads nothing by provenance
findings.problem: Configuration B learns on fresh1, whose 33 instances are first stages by construction (467 tasks), and on corpus partitions that hold the same (routine, parameter) instances as FRESH-2's stages. The deepening loop turns a teacher's solution of one learning task into a symbol; that is what 'targets first' is for. It spends up to 10^6 candidates on that one instance and gets a hidden-example verdict in every run (FRESH-1 has 1 or 2 hidden examples per task). A FRESH-4 task with that instance as a stage is then close to a one-stage task for the trained arm, and each instance recurs in about 15 FRESH-4 tasks. A lead built this way means 'cached solutions of training tasks are reused where the same instance reappears'. The claim sentence ('new two-stage tasks') and the bullet 'New pairings of the stage instances of FRESH-1 and FRESH-2' do not convey that, and no ending or stratum separates it from help on stages the loop never trained on. Only 76 tasks have no learning instance; 119 contain a routine that no learning task has.
findings.evidence:
Same directory: <work>/confounds.
- a_generator.py: 'FRESH-4 tasks whose first stage is a FRESH-1 task instance: 467 | whose second stage is also a FRESH-1 task instance: 188 | both: 86'; 'first-stage instances 65 second-stage instances 69'.
- b_overlap.py: by function on the pool 'both 424 | first only 426 | second only 74 | neither 76'; by name 'both 415 | first only 435 | second only 72 | neither 78'; 'first-stage routines with no learning task of the family: {pow-base-k: 14, dedup: 22, sort: 24}'; second stage '{pow-base-k: 20, dedup: 28, sort: 10, is-evens: 1, is-squares: 1, len: 1}'.
- What the symbols are, toy loop on exposed partitions only (d_taint.py, student 300, teacher at most 2,000; table printed by e_taint_compare.py): 5 of 6 accepted symbols are one learning task's whole verified program, e.g. 's2_1 accepted True gain 43 tasks 6 real 1 targets 1 | (lambda x0: list[int]. ((index (length (tail x0))) x0))', 's3_1 ... real 1 targets 1 | ((cons ((index 2) x0)) x0)', and 's1_1 ... real 1 targets 1 | filter (if (eq x1 5) true (is_prime (add x1 4)))', an overfitted fusion accepted because the verified score rose.

((cons (head x0)) ((cons ((mul 2) 5)) (tail (tail x0))))', which is replace-index-2-with-10 with its constants.
- f_mix.py: 'fresh1 tasks 33 hidden examples per task {1: 17, 2: 16}'.
findings.proposed_change: Fix these strata now, from data only. Rule: a stage instance 'is a learning task' when its function under the validated reading equals a learning task's validated reference on the whole 866-input pool. Strata: both stages (424), one (500), none (76); and 'contains a routine no learning task has' (119: pow-base-k, dedup, sort, is-evens, is-squares, len). confirm.py asserts the counts and prints, for each stratum, the primary comparison, new against old and solves per arm, graded none / not separated / significant. Add to 'What FRESH-4 is and is not' and to the licence: 'in 924 of 1,000 tasks at least one stage, and in 850 the first stage, is a routine instance the loop trained on with verifier verdicts; a positive result is about re-pairing those instances unless the 76-task and 119-task strata show a lead of their own'. Change the claim sentence from 'new two-stage tasks' to 'new pairings of routine instances, most of them its own learning tasks'.

findings.title: 440 of the 1,000 tasks repeat the routine pair of a FRESH-3 task; the independence rule the Addendum 7 review imposed for FRESH-2 was not carried over
findings.problem: FRESH-3 is a development set now: the redesign was read off its results by routine and two variants were compared on it. fresh4.py still excludes only FRESH-2's routine pairs (used_pairs, line 47). 440 FRESH-4 tasks have the routine pair of a FRESH-3 task with other parameters. Every first-stage instance and the second-stage instance of 991 tasks occur in FRESH-3 in the same position. About 460 tasks contain a routine family the Addendum-7 loop never solved, which are the families the redesign was aimed at. A positive result therefore means that the loop, as redesigned on these routines, repairs them on other pairings of the same 65 + 69 instances. It cannot show that the procedure works on a routine population it was not fitted to. The draft does say 'FRESH-3 guided the design; FRESH-4 comes from the same population of pairs', but no analysis reads the tasks farthest from the development sets.

Add a fifth ending, decided mechanically on the 560 tasks whose pair of routine names neither FRESH-2 nor FRESH-3 has: 'only on routine pairs a development set has' / 'on new routine pairs not separated from chance' / 'also on routine pairs no development set has', with its own prediction. Say in the licence that the mechanism was fitted to this routine population. Alternative that matches the Addendum 7 rule: add FRESH-3's routine pairs to used_pairs and regenerate (2,176 candidates, about 1,100 expected to pass, so COUNT of 1,000 leaves almost no reserve; 800 leaves one). The strata of the previous finding (76 and 119 tasks) are the only analysis available here for 'more than new pairings of the same instances'.

findings.title: The list-only scope is in two bullets but not in the claim sentence, the outcome string or the reading of D6
findings.problem: Addendum 7's review replaced a 283/8/9 draft set by quotas because S and R act on list outputs only. FRESH-4 is 964/28/8, more list-heavy than that rejected draft, and Addendum 7's ending 'for list outputs only' is gone. Quotas are not possible on what is left, so restricting the claim is the right treatment. But the restriction is carried only by prose. The claim under test says 'new two-stage tasks'. outcome_class() prints 'confirmed on FRESH-4 against everything generation 0 solves at any budget run' with four endings, none of which carries it. D6 calls old against generation 0 'the comparison of Addendum 7 on more tasks', although the share of the stratum where old led (62 against 55 on list, 9 against 9 elsewhere) rose from 71% to 96%; a pass would read as overturning 'not established'. The 36 other tasks cannot inform either way: 26 of them are exact compositions of two learning tasks, and D11's 'within 3' is noise.

findings.proposed_change: (1) Claim sentence: '... solve more new two-stage tasks with list output ...'. (2) Decide the class and the endings on the 964 list-output tasks, report the 36 others apart, and start the outcome string with 'for list outputs (964 of 1,000 tasks)'. (3) Reword D6 and the secondary line: 'old against generation 0 on a set that is 96% list outputs (FRESH-3: 71%); a pass does not change the outcome class of Addendum 7'; print that comparison on list outputs beside FRESH-3's 62 against 55 of 213. (4) Print the lead standardised to FRESH-2's mix (0.71 / 0.11 / 0.18 of the per-type solve rates) beside the raw lead, marked as resting on 28 and 8 tasks.

findings.title: 'What has run on it: nothing' holds for the examples, not for the functions: 18 FRESH-4 generating pairs are in the smoke set that replicate.py --tiny runs
findings.problem: fresh4.py excludes only the 300 registered FRESH-3 pairs. The 60-task smoke set of Addendum 7 (fresh3.SMOKE_SEED), which solvers run at toy budgets in every replicate.py --tiny, shares 18 generating pairs with FRESH-4, with other inputs. The README had to disclose the same thing for FRESH-3 after the fact (9 pairs, two of them among the trained-only solves). The discarded Addendum 7 draft set (digest 333e3506..., 300 pairs from the same candidates, run at up to 9,948 candidates) cannot be rebuilt from the tree, so its overlap with FRESH-4 is unknown.

Have confirm.py list the 18 keys and print the primary comparison without them. State whether the pairs of the discarded draft set can be recovered; if they can, treat them the same way.

reviews.coverage:
All work is in <work>/confounds (scripts, logs, fresh_cache.json). No solver ran on a FRESH-4 task and no solver-made program was evaluated on a FRESH-4 example. Solver runs were on exposed partitions only, at most 2,000 candidates, 2 workers.

What held:
- **Generator (gen_cache.py, a_generator.py).** fresh4.make() reproduces the full digest d54c6593...a64b4 and every stated count: 3,410 candidates, 1,669 examined, 1,000 made, 964/28/8, empty public input 367, negative value 141, median 9, divisibility 332, slice-k-n 73 (first stage only; it never occurs as a second stage).
- **References.** All 1,000 tasks' 16 examples equal stage 2 after stage 1 under the validated readings. Each task has 16 distinct inputs, all from the 866-input pool. No FRESH-3 pair and no FRESH-2 routine pair occurs.
- **Exclusions, re-checked independently.** No task is reproduced by any validated reading of an exposed task, by a FRESH-3 reference or by an earlier FRESH-4 reference. In the direction the rule does not check: 2 tasks are reproduced by a later FRESH-4 reference, and 27 exposed and 4 FRESH-3 tasks' own examples are reproduced by some FRESH-4 reference. Negligible.
- **Degenerate pipelines (b_overlap.py).** One stage alone reproduces all 16 examples in 7 tasks and the 8 public examples in 31; 21 tasks have at most 2 distinct outputs. Small.
- **Leak paths, static trace.** In deepen.run, measure() builds programs and score from learning partitions only. The report runs' return values are discarded except the run number. The timeline is read only for ceilings, spent and counts. The dream-only run passes partition_names=() and runs no real task. Harness.default ignores added partitions. T_new includes the report runs.
- **Leak paths, mutation test (d_taint.py, e_taint_compare.py).** A toy loop with a stand-in partition added before the loop, as confirm.py does, was run twice, once with every held-out row replaced by garbage. Result: same 16 calls, 'a run named the added partition: False', library, cycles and all 13 decisive timeline records identical, while the report records differ (held-out counts 1 against 23). I found no path from a held-out verdict to a decision.
- **Hidden examples of learning tasks.** They steer the loop on learning tasks only (targets, score, corpus). I found no path to FRESH-4 outputs. In 21 of the 467 tasks whose first stage is a FRESH-1 task, one example input is that task's own hidden input (10 hidden and 11 public examples in all). The verified score that gates symbols is not a sound score: the toy run accepted an overfitted teacher program as a symbol. That can only hurt the trained arm on FRESH-4.
- **Input overlap with dreams (c_dream_sim.py).** 948 of 16,000 FRESH-4 example inputs are in the 300-input dream pool; 5,931 are public inputs of some learning task. Not material.
- **Mix inside list outputs (f_mix.py).** S applies to the raw input in 133 of 964 list tasks, against 37 of 213 in FRESH-3. Similar.

Not done:
- confirm.py --tiny end to end: its control rungs (2,500 and 3,000) and teacher cap (5,000) exceed the 2,000-candidate limit.
- The reserve was not generated.
- The dream estimates use the Addendum-7 loop's 154 learning programs as a stand-in corpus, because the deepening loop's own report is not in the tree.

Outside my lens, noticed in passing: confirm.py scores P1-P12, which is not the registered list D1-D11. D3, D9 and D11 are not scored, and P1, P2, P11 and P12 are not registered.

reviews.round: second round (draft at commit 4ace9d8, after the first round's changes; another model)

findings.title: An empty or tiny stratum is read as an absence claim, and the size of ending 4's stratum is not fixed in advance
findings.problem: graded() returns 'none' whenever trained <= control. That includes an empty stratum (paired(set(), set()) gives 0 vs 0) and a stratum with almost no discordant tasks. outcome_class then prints an absence claim such as 'not where no dream computed the task or composed its pair of routines' or 'only where both stages are its own learning tasks'. The draft says 'A stratum is small where stated', but none of the five endings is marked small. Ending 4's stratum (scope - dreamt_keys) depends on the run, so its size is unknown before the run, and it is the one most likely to be small. Dreams are balanced over routine families, 400 per cycle. FRESH-4 has 295 ordered routine pairs among its list tasks, and 621 of the 756 list tasks have both routines in learning families. A few cycles of dreams cover most family pairs, so the undreamt stratum shrinks towards the 135 list tasks with an unmet routine (roughly 150-250 tasks). That stratum is close to the same set as the D10 stratum, so D7 and D10 are nearly redundant. Power, assuming the development effect applies uniformly (optimistic, because on FRESH-3 the earlier lead outside the divisibility family was 5 vs 5): ending 1 (494 tasks) and ending 5 (448 tasks) are at least 0.99 at half the development effect. A 200-task stratum is 0.81 at half and 0.35 at the Addendum 7 effect. The 135-task unmet stratum is 0.64 at half and 0.25 at the Addendum 7 effect. The 62-task 'none' stratum is 0.29 at half, and a true effect reads 'none' in 9% of draws (26% at the Addendum 7 effect).
findings.evidence: confirm.py lines 156-159 (graded) and 590 ('undreamt': within(scope - dreamt_keys)). I ran fresh4.make() and provenance as data (work/statistics/gen.py -> f4.json): list 756; outside the earlier routines 494; not both stages learning tasks 448; none 62; unmet 135; 295 ordered pairs; 621 tasks with both routines in learning families. work/statistics/power.py (4000 draws, exact sign test from replicate.py), (power, P(reads 'none')): dev 36/7 per 213: n=200 (0.999, 0), n=135 (0.973, 0), n=62 (0.724, 0.008); half 21.5/7: n=494 (0.994, 0), n=448 (0.987, 0), n=200 (0.809, 0.005), n=135 (0.638, 0.015), n=62 (0.293, 0.09); A7 14/7: n=494 (0.722, 0.011), n=200 (0.345, 0.087), n=135 (0.247, 0.13), n=62 (0.077, 0.261).
findings.proposed_change: Add a fourth grade to graded(): 'not testable' when the stratum has fewer than 10 discordant tasks (or fewer than 100 tasks), with the wording '<ending> not testable: N tasks, D discordant'. Use it in all five endings and in D4/D7/D8/D10 (score those as 'not scored'). Register that the 'none' wording is used only when the stratum is testable. In the registration, state ending 4's size as unknown before the run and give the power table above for each ending's stratum.

findings.title: 'How many routines carry the lead' measures loss of power, not concentration; 'short' is undefined
findings.problem: The procedure removes routines in a fixed order of net lead (computed once, not recomputed) and stops as soon as the remaining lead loses p < 0.05. Each removal also drops every task that contains the routine (2 routines per task, 27 routines), so n falls quickly and significance is lost even when the effect is spread evenly. I simulated an effect spread evenly over all routines. At the Addendum 7 effect size the lead is 'carried by' 1-3 routines in 70% of draws. At half the development effect it is 3-8 routines, which overlaps the result for an effect confined to tasks containing one of 3 routines (2-3 routines). The draft's rule 'If the list is short, the report says that the lead holds over pairs of these routines and claims nothing for the others' therefore cannot tell a broad effect from a narrow one, and 'short' is chosen after the result. A stricter stop (remaining lead <= 0) separates better at large effects but still overlaps at small ones.
findings.evidence: confirm.py lines 458-472 (order fixed once; stop when graded != 'significant'). work/statistics/carry.py on the FRESH-4 list-task structure, 200 draws each, routines removed: uniform dev 36/7: 8-21 (median about 13, about 124 tasks left); uniform half 21.5/7: mostly 3-11 (about 351 tasks left); uniform A7 14/7: {1: 68, 2: 38, 3: 35, 4: 21, ...} (about 604 tasks left); all wins in tasks with one of 3 routines: {2: 61, 3: 131, ...}. carry0.py with the stop rule 'lead <= 0': uniform A7 still gives 1-5 routines in 70 of 200 draws.
findings.proposed_change: Change the wording to 'removing routines in a fixed order of net lead, k routines and their tasks (n tasks left) take the lead out of significance'. Always report, beside it, the lead per task (new-only minus control-only, divided by tasks) inside the removed tasks and in the remaining tasks. Replace 'if the list is short' with a fixed rule: the report says the lead holds over pairs of these routines only if the remaining tasks show no lead (trained <= control) and number at least 200. Otherwise it says 'the count of routines is not evidence of narrowness'. Say in the text that the order is computed once.

findings.title: predictions() scores D3 at 80 where the table says 50; D10's scope is ambiguous
findings.problem: The table defines D3 as 'The lead of D1 is at least 50 sound solves'. predictions() uses THRESHOLDS['D3_lead'] = 80, which is marked 'provisional until the registration is in force'. A lead between 50 and 79 would be scored FAIL against the registered wording. D10's text does not say 'list outputs', and the draft quotes 141 tasks for this stratum (all outputs). The code scores it on the list scope (135 tasks).
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md line 794 ('at least 50'); confirm.py line 649 and line 663 'THRESHOLDS = {"D3_lead": 80}        # provisional until the registration is in force'; confirm.py line 644 uses strata[...], which are restricted to scope (line 423); f4.json: unmet routine in 141 tasks overall, 135 among list tasks.
findings.proposed_change: Set one value in both the table and THRESHOLDS before the registration is frozen, and drop the 'provisional' comment. Reword D10 as 'list outputs (135 tasks)'. Have the script print the D3 threshold it used beside the score.

findings.title: The ending-5 stratum size is wrong, and the licence's escape clause ('unless the fifth ending and the finer strata show a lead of their own') is undefined
findings.problem: Ending 5 is registered as '(386 list-output tasks)'. The code takes stages < 2, which on the registered set is 448 list tasks (386 with one learning-task stage plus 62 with none). The 386 is the 'one' cell. The licence says the result would not license 'more than re-pairing of routine instances the loop trained on, unless the fifth ending and the finer strata show a lead of their own'. Two problems follow. First, the fifth ending's stratum is mostly tasks in which one stage is a learning task, so a significant fifth ending still does not show anything beyond trained instances. Second, the finer strata 'decide nothing' and have no rule for what 'a lead of their own' means: the 'none' stratum is 62 tasks with power 0.29 at half the development effect. That leaves the reading open after the result.
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md lines 704-705 and 778-780; confirm.py lines 435 and 590; work/statistics f4.json: list provenance Counter({1: 386, 2: 308, 0: 62}).
findings.proposed_change: Correct the stratum size to 448 (386 + 62). Replace the clause with a mechanical rule: the result licenses something beyond re-pairing of trained instances only if the 'no stage instance is a learning task' stratum (62 list tasks) or the 'a routine no learning task has' stratum (135 list tasks) is 'significant' by graded(). State that these strata have low power (figures above), so that 'not separated' there is not read as absence. Otherwise drop 'unless ...' altogether.

findings.title: R2 as defined no longer contains the original's ablation of a symbol of an earlier generation
findings.problem: The original R2 is 'a gain of generation >= 2 depends on a symbol of an earlier generation (ablation loses it)'. The draft ablates the 'recursive symbols': symbols accepted in cycle >= 2 whose support meets a discovery, together with their textual descendants. The FRESH-4 gain must be lost when those are removed. With two accepting cycles, that shows the final generation's gain depends on a symbol of the same generation. The link to an earlier generation is only historical: the discovering teacher used some learned symbol. Nothing requires the recursive symbol to be defined through an earlier symbol, and the teacher's programs are inlined before they leave the engine. Nothing requires the gain to be lost when the earlier symbols are removed. The two plain ablations that would test that ('without-cycle1-lineage', 'without-cycle1-only') are computed but are not part of R2. In one respect the draft's R2 is stricter (it needs the chain). In the respect the original states explicitly it is weaker, so the claim 'This is stricter than the reading used for the earlier loops' is not true in every respect. R2 also needs only one task.
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md lines 26 and 745-756; confirm.py lines 301-303 (seeds from info['support'] & through; the recursive set does not need an earlier-cycle ancestor), 518-525 (second(): lost = uses - solved(ablated_label) for the without-recursive row only), 306 (the lineage ablations, reported only).
findings.proposed_change: Additionally require, in second(), that the task is also lost in 'new-without-cycle1-lineage@student:fresh4', or more generally without the earlier-cycle symbols that the discovery's teacher program used ('used' of that teacher record). Alternatively require every seed symbol to be in descendants(library, symbols of earlier cycles). Report the number of tasks meeting R2, not only 'holds'. Reword the line about strictness as 'stricter in the chain it requires; R2 holds only if the gain is also lost without the earlier symbols'.

findings.title: Outcomes the table does not cover, plus an untested ending and a wording dependency
findings.problem: (a) No reading is given for a registered loop that does not reproduce LOOP-NUMBERS: the text says it 'repeats the last development run'. (b) If C2new > MEMORY_LIMIT, the script stops with SystemExit before any FRESH-4 run. The table does not say this means 'no class', or whether a rerun is allowed. (c) The claim sentence ('up to 1,126,452 ... which is more than the whole training and deployment budget') is true only if TOP >= C2new; C2new is still pending. (d) Ending 3 is decided on raw counts (new-only kind (a) > control-only kind (a)), with no test, so 5 vs 4 reads 'with reach beyond the budget'. The p-value is computed in kinds_of but not used. D9 is rated PASS (high) on the same raw rule. (e) row['thin_evidence'] counts every program with fewer than 20 checked inputs. checked stops counting at the first disagreement, so unsound programs that fail early are counted as 'removed by the 20-input rule' and the reported number is too high. The rule itself treats the arms equally, because the in-domain count depends only on the task.
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md lines 563-564, 543-546, 697-699; confirm.py lines 222-223 (SystemExit), 588 (budget_bound_lead raw), replicate.py lines 144-149 (p computed, unused), confirm.py lines 81-92 and 324-325 (checked counts only up to the first failure; thin_evidence uses seen < MIN_EVIDENCE regardless of ok).
findings.proposed_change: Add these rows to the table. 'The loop's library digest or training ceiling differs from LOOP-NUMBERS: the class is read as registered, and the report states the difference.' 'C2new exceeds the memory limit: no class; no rerun under this registration.' Make the claim sentence read 'up to max(1,126,452, C2new)', or state the inequality as a checked condition. Grade ending 3 like the others with graded() on budget_bound (none / not separated / significant), and score D9 the same way. Count thin evidence only for programs that agree on all checked inputs (ok and seen < 20).

findings.title: R2's 'recursive symbol' test checks the task key, not the discovering program, and ignores timing
findings.problem: confirm.py marks a symbol as recursive when `info['cycle'] >= 2 and set(info['support']) & through`. Here `through` is the union of discovery task keys from every later cycle, and `support` is the set of learning-task keys whose current corpus program the symbol folds. Neither check matches what Addendum 8 asks for ('the discovery is one of the learning programs it folds'). (i) `absorb` keeps the smaller program per key. If an earlier teacher already solved the task, the corpus can still hold that older program, which uses no symbol, while a later teacher re-solves the same task with a symbol. The symbol then folds the old program, yet it is counted as distilled from the discovery. (ii) A discovery made by the teacher of cycle 4 can certify a symbol accepted in cycle 2, before that discovery existed. Either path loosens the R2 chain that the control-fairness review tightened, and R2 feeds D12 and D14.
findings.evidence: In the tiny loop (work/implementation/loopA.json, cycle 2), 23 of the 24 tasks the cycle-2 teacher solved had already been solved by the cycle-1 teacher. Targets recur from cycle to cycle, so the same key often has both an older corpus program and a newer teacher program. Both accepted cycle-2 symbols (s7_1, s12_1) have support tasks that are in teacher1 and also in teacher2. confirm.py lines 283-303: `through |= with_symbols` takes keys from all cycles, and `seeds` is tested against `info['support']`, which lists keys only. The 'support' field in deepen.py line 303 records keys but not the programs folded.
findings.proposed_change: In deepen.py, record for each trial the text of the folded program of every support task: `'support_programs': {t: str(full[t]) for t in symbol.tasks if t in family_of}`. In confirm.py, keep discoveries per cycle. A symbol accepted in cycle c becomes a seed only if, for some support key k, k was discovered by the teacher of some cycle c' <= c, and `support_programs[k] == by_run[cycles[c'-1]['teacher_run']]['programs'][k][0]`.

findings.title: D3 is scored at a lead of 80; the registered table says 50
findings.problem: The D table in Addendum 8 gives D3 as 'The lead of D1 is at least 50 sound solves'. predictions() in confirm.py scores D3 as `primary['trained'] - primary['control'] >= THRESHOLDS['D3_lead']`, and THRESHOLDS = {'D3_lead': 80}, marked 'provisional'. A lead between 50 and 79 would be scored FAIL against a registered PASS prediction.
findings.evidence: confirm.py line 649 (D3 uses THRESHOLDS['D3_lead']) and line 663 (`THRESHOLDS = {"D3_lead": 80}        # provisional until the registration is in force`). PREDICTIONS.md line 794: '| D3 | The lead of D1 is at least 50 sound solves | PASS (moderate) |'.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one number before registration and write the same number in both places: either set THRESHOLDS['D3_lead'] = 50, or change the D3 row to 80. Remove the 'provisional' comment.

findings.title: Ending 5's stratum is 448 list-output tasks, not the 386 the draft states
findings.problem: Ending 5 and D8 are read on 'the tasks in which not both stage instances are learning tasks (386 list-output tasks)'. The code uses `origin[key]['stages'] < 2`, which on the generated set gives 448 list-output tasks. 386 is the number with exactly one learning-task stage. The other 62 are the 'none' list tasks, which the draft itself counts in its finer strata. The registered size and the registered rule disagree, so a reader cannot tell which stratum decides ending 5.
findings.evidence: work/implementation/f4.py ran fresh4.make() and fresh4.provenance() as data, with no solver. It printed: 'list not-both 448 list none 62' (so exactly-one = 386), 'prov both 336 one 400 none 64 first 673 unmet 141'. Output was identical under PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 7, digest 6159d55f...abb9c. confirm.py lines 435 and 590 use `stages < 2`.
findings.proposed_change: Change '386 list-output tasks' to '448 list-output tasks' in ending 5. If 'exactly one stage is a learning task' was meant, change the code to `== 1` and the wording to match.

findings.title: thin_evidence counts unsound programs, not the programs MIN_EVIDENCE removes
findings.problem: Sound._agrees returns at the first disagreement with the number of inputs checked so far. A program that is wrong on its 5th fresh input therefore has seen = 5 < 20 and is listed in row['thin_evidence']. The registration says the report gives 'the number of programs this [the 20-input rule] removes'. The reported number includes programs that are unsound on ample evidence and that the rule did not remove.
findings.evidence: work/implementation/thin.py on the --tiny output. The only thin_evidence entries (gen0@top:fresh4, gen0@C2new:fresh4: fresh3::((add-k ... -2)) (prepend-k ...)) have verdict (False, 5), with 200 of 200 in-domain fresh inputs available. The MIN_EVIDENCE rule removed nothing, yet the report says 1 per row.
findings.proposed_change: In confirm.py, line 324: `row['thin_evidence'] = sorted(key for key, (ok, seen) in verdicts.items() if seen is not None and seen < MIN_EVIDENCE and not ok and <program agreed on all inputs it saw>)`. Simplest: make `verdict` return a third field `agrees` and count `agrees and seen < MIN_EVIDENCE`.

findings.title: --resume never keeps ablation or per-cycle rows (the fingerprint holds a tuple)
findings.problem: For an ablated or per-cycle vocabulary, measure() builds `fingerprint['state'] = state`, which is the tuple (label, kept-library dict). After the JSON round trip it is a list, so `rows[label].get('fingerprint') == fingerprint` is never true. Those rows are always rerun on resume. The results do not change, because the runs are deterministic. But the behaviour contradicts the registered 'a finished evaluation row is kept if...', and it costs repeated runs at 10^4 on 800 + 338 tasks.
findings.evidence: thin.py printed 'fingerprint state type after JSON: list' for rows['cycle1@student:fresh4']. confirm.py line 237 has `"state": state` and line 240 compares against the JSON-loaded value.
findings.proposed_change: Use `"state": state if isinstance(state, str) else state[0]` in the fingerprint. The 'library' field, sorted(state[1]), already identifies the vocabulary.

reviews.coverage:
Work directory: <work>/implementation. No solver touched a FRESH-4 task. fresh4 was only generated and read as data.

These checks held:

**Determinism**
- I ran the tiny loop (deepen.py B --tiny --max-cycles 2) twice: PYTHONHASHSEED=1 with 2 workers, and PYTHONHASHSEED=7 with 1 worker. The two reports are identical apart from the seconds fields.
- fresh4.make() under PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 7 gives identical output with the registered digest 6159d55f97e57301dc91eb5a58247294c054eb613c873c10149dc68b192abb9c: 2,040 candidates, 1,670 examined, 800 made, 756/37/7 by output type.

**FRESH-4 exclusions and statistics**
- 0 tasks repeat a routine-name pair of FRESH-2 or FRESH-3.
- 0 pipelines overlap FRESH-3, the 60-task smoke set or the 300 draft pipelines, and there are no duplicates.
- Provenance: 336/400/64 by learning-task stages, 673 first-stage, 141 unmet (dedup, len, pow-base-k, sort).
- 236 divisibility tasks, 39 slice-k-n, 317 empty / 91 negative / median 8. All match the draft.
- Stage routine names match the learning families from partitions.family, except those four unmet routines. So dream_pairs, outside_dreams and provenance compare like with like, and in dreams f is the first stage.

**deepen.run, line by line**
- Teacher share = min(CAP, 214*TEACHER // |unsolved|), run with only=unsolved. Ceilings are share x |unsolved|, and T_new sums teacher, trial (including gate dream jobs), dream and report runs.
- Phase 1 put-offs do not count as trials. Three rejections in a row move to phase 2, or end it.
- tabu persists across cycles; put_off resets each cycle.
- A rejected candidate carries no state: library, corpus, solved_now and score are unchanged, and the next proposal comes from the same `full` plus the corpus.
- The gate uses exact Fractions and a strict or tie-break comparison. The cycle, trial and support fields are correct in the tiny run.
- Stop and checkpoint order is correct.
- No decision reads a held-out record: family_score, solved_now, corpus and the input pool use learning partitions only, and held = ALL minus learn, so the added fresh4/fresh3 partitions are never run by the loop.

**Dreamer**
- Public and check examples are disjoint (distinct pool inputs). 'taken' is shared, so the gate, target and corpus samples are disjoint.
- An empty focus yields no pairs; this does not crash.

**Harness.run(only=...)**
- Rows and verifier queries come only from the chosen tasks. Partitions with zero chosen tasks give empty lists and summary() gives 0. With only=None the behaviour is unchanged.

**confirm.py**
- The digest check comes before the loop, though it compares only the first 16 hex digits.
- C2old = 259,100, and C2new and C1new follow the registered formulas.
- The union 'any' holds 5 rungs on FRESH-4 and every held-out rung plus C1new on held-out B. gen0, new and old differ only in library: spec_without on the JSON library round-trips every witness, definition and dream program through parse/str in the tiny run.
- descendants, the ablations, and the per-cycle rows with only one cycle row work. No KeyError when nothing is recursive: the R2 lookup is guarded by `if recursive`.
- The tie-break flag logic follows the gate. Scope = list everywhere the class and endings are decided. The other predictions map correctly to the D table. kinds is read at the top rung (1,126,452 whenever C2new is smaller).
- `confirm.py --tiny` ran end to end in about 3 minutes and printed a class.

**File size and memory at real scale**
- The tiny output is 1 MB for 60 tasks. Rows plus a 12-cycle timeline are estimated at tens of MB, which is not a problem.

**Not checked**
- Behaviour at budgets of 10^5 and above (memory and executor). The rule against large runs forbids it.
